one_liner: PyTorch C++/CUDA extension for batched parallel rANS coding, pitched as a faster replacement for torchac and CompressAI range coding.
what_it_does: Encodes and decodes int32 symbol tensors with rANS, where each symbol picks its own quantized CDF row by index, as learned (neural) compression models need. Exposes low-level tensor operators (rans64/rans32/rans32_16 init_stream, push, pop, with i2/i4/i8/i32 interleaved, alias and inverse-CDF variants) and a high-level TorchANSInterface whose init_params/encode_with_indexes/decode_with_indexes calls mirror CompressAI's entropy coder. It is not a drop-in for CompressAI's RansEncoder bitstream format; streams come back as a (B, L) int32 tensor or a list of bytes.
how_it_is_fast: Each batch row is an independent rANS stream coded in parallel (OpenMP at::parallel_for on CPU, one thread or one warp per row on CUDA). The rans32_16 32-way path maps 32 interleaved states onto the lanes of a warp with a shared bitstream cursor placed by __ballot_sync/__popc/__shfl_sync accounting (technique credited to Recoil), and stages whole CDF rows plus a sparse inverse-CDF table in shared memory. The CPU coder uses branch-free renormalization, a pipelined floating-point divide with an integer fix-up, register-resident interleaved states, and a sparse 2^q inverse-CDF lookup table with a bounded branch-free walk.
when_to_use: Learned image/video compression in PyTorch where many symbols each use a different, model-predicted distribution and you want entropy coding on the same device as the network

Large GPU batches (about 2048+ rows on a 68-SM GPU) with freq_precision <= 15, using rans32_16 + num_interleaves=32 + inverse_cdf_precision="auto" for the measured ~26 Gsymbol/s raw decode on an RTX 2080 Ti
CPU coding of batched tensors where rans64/rans32 with num_interleaves=4 and the auto inverse-CDF table give several hundred Msymbol/s per operator (benchmark_status.md, i7-6800K)
Research prototyping of rANS variants (state/stream/precision sizes, alias vs inverse-CDF lookup) behind one Python API
when_not_to_use: You need a proven win over torchac or CompressAI: the repo never benchmarks against either, nor against DietGPU, so the speedup over the named baseline is unmeasured

Small or per-image calls through the high-level API on CUDA: the committed end-to-end numbers are only 1.7-8.7 Msymbol/s decode (256 x 8192 symbols, including stream/bytes conversion), thousands of times below the raw-kernel figures
Non-PyTorch C++ projects: the coder is built as a torch extension (torch/extension.h, at::parallel_for) and needs a local compiler, plus a matching nvcc for CUDA
Production or untrusted inputs: the README calls it research-purpose software where segfaults may occur with the low-level API, and out-of-range symbols beyond about 2^30 are silently mis-coded
Interleaved coding of rans64/rans32 on GPU (CPU-only), or 32-way interleaving on CPU (slower than 4-way per the README)

integration.dependencies: PyTorch (>= 1.10 recommended), pybind11, a C++17 compiler, ninja for the runtime build, OpenMP for CPU parallelism; CUDA toolkit matching torch.version.cuda for GPU
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (torch 2.x selects its own standard); Python >= 3.7; nvcc >= 12.2 or g++ <= 10 host compiler when libstdc++ is from GCC >= 11.4
integration.platforms: Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/arm64, Windows x86_64; CUDA on NVIDIA GPUs; ROCm untested
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: TorchANSInterface mimics CompressAI's entropy coder API, but the bitstream is its own format and torchac's API is not mirrored

gotchas: On x86_64 setup.py adds -march=native, so a built extension may not run on an older CPU than the build machine.
CUDA support is opt-in at build time (WITH_CUDA=1); a CPU-only build asked to code CUDA tensors warns and compiles a CUDA extension on the spot, which takes minutes.
Interleaved streams reserve one word of slack because renormalization stores speculatively past the cursor; the README warns that misuse of the low-level API can segfault.

The 4-way CUDA interleaved path decoded wrong symbols in v0.2.1 (benchmark_status.md marks it 'broken'; fixed in v0.3.0), and a Known Issue says the rans64 CUDA test fails on some newer GPU architectures.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over DietGPU or Recoil when you need per-symbol distribution indexes, bypass coding of out-of-range int32 values and a PyTorch tensor API rather than raw byte or fixed-width-symbol buffers; pick constriction instead for single-stream CPU coding with exact model control outside PyTorch, and DietGPU for maximum raw GB/s on data-center GPUs.
verified_claims_summary: First-party only: on an i7-6800K and RTX 2080 Ti (torch 2.11.0+cu130), raw rans32_16 32-way CUDA kernels reach 27.8 Gsymbol/s encode and 25.7-26.4 Gsymbol/s decode, CPU 4-way operators 0.4-0.9 Gsymbol/s, and v0.3.0 beats v0.2.1 by 1.27x-2.75x on CPU decode. Every comparison is against its own earlier release or its own lookup variants; no torchac, CompressAI or DietGPU numbers are given, and no compiler version is stated (setup.py uses -O3 -fopenmp -march=native).
status_note: Actively developed (v0.3.0 released 2026-09-14, 74 commits, 6 stars), MIT-licensed, but self-described as research software with no prebuilt wheels.
